examples.title: A song, from a caption and lyrics
examples.why: The one capability that is not optional, so this is the example to read first. It is the exact request behind docs/demo/demo-song.mp3, and the shape of that caption is most of what decides the quality.
examples.recoveredFrom: ~/.aiplay-studio/library.json → meta['aiplay_00060.flac'], which is what the render itself wrote. The mp3 is docs/demo/demo-song.mp3, transcoded from that FLAC by scripts/demos.mjs.
examples.teaches: The caption is three labelled parts — Global Metadata, Vocal Details, Arrangement. Lyrics carry [Verse] / [Chorus] / [Bridge] tags, and song LENGTH follows lyric length: the same request with an empty lyrics box stops after about 30 seconds.

examples.title: Starting from a real song — the strength dial, three settings
examples.why: The same reference at three denoise values, so the cliff is audible rather than asserted. This is the control people most often set wrong.
examples.recoveredFrom: docs/demo/manifest.json, written by scripts/demos.mjs, which measured each file before shipping it. The caption and the reference recording are NOT recorded anywhere and are not guessed at here.

measured.denoise 0.60: Denoise 0.60 — still a copy. r = 0.94 against the near-copy end of the dial.
measured.denoise 0.85: Denoise 0.85 — the shipped default. Waveform correlation has collapsed to 0.004: a new performance.
measured.denoise 0.95: Denoise 0.95 — past the useful range; the reference stops steering it.

examples.teaches: 0.85 is the shipped default and the only setting that is a genuine blend. Below 0.80 you get a copy; at 0.90 and above the trim removes less than one step and the reference stops steering anything.

examples.title: A video clip, prompt in
examples.why: Five seconds of 1280x704 with its own audio track. The request here is not a reconstruction — it is the graph ComfyUI was handed, read back out of the mp4.
examples.recoveredFrom: The mp4's own `prompt` metadata tag — the executed graph, verbatim. It also identifies the file as the first output of scripts/ltx_smoke.mjs (filename_prefix `clips/ltx`, the same two-pass sigmas).

measured.renderNote: 121 s measured on a 16 GB RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (config.js, video engines).

examples.teaches: LTX's frame count is fps x seconds + 1 — 121, not 120. H3's rule is different (n mod 17 == 5), which is why the two engines are not interchangeable and Studio refuses a mismatched size rather than rounding it.

examples.title: A picture that uses two other pictures
examples.why: FLUX.2 klein's reference images are how a character stays the same character across pictures, and the Images screen has no attach control for them yet — so this example is the documentation for a feature you can otherwise only find in the API.
examples.recoveredFrom: The output PNG's own tEXt graph names its two LoadImage inputs. Those staged files were sha256-compared against the gallery and are byte-identical to imtb3bfdj.png (sha256:d1f0cfa29fdcd644…, slot 1) and imtb3b0ud.png (sha256:f8ca6b60cf4f121b…, slot 2) — so the ordering here is proven, not inferred from timestamps.

referencePrompts.ref-1-portrait.png: portrait of a young woman with short dark hair, plain grey background, no hat, neutral expression
referencePrompts.ref-2-red-hat.png: a single wide-brimmed red felt hat on a plain white background, product photo, centred

examples.teaches: The two reference pictures are themselves examples: each was made from one plain sentence. The composite's prompt never describes the face or the hat — it points at them. That is the whole technique.

examples.title: A production bible, and one scene it rendered
examples.why: The music-video pipeline's eleven stages all read one document. This is a real one, whole — the smallest complete project on this machine — beside a clip it produced.
examples.recoveredFrom: The project document as saved, with no absolute paths in it (asserted at build time). The scene prompt is the mp4's own `prompt` tag — the graph ComfyUI ran — not a re-derivation from the bible.
examples.teaches: Read the chain: `brief` and `styleBible` set the look once; `boards[2].boardPrompt` is "The boat alone in the garden under frost"; the clip prompt that reached the engine is the style line, then the named references as `<Picture 1>` / `<Picture 2>`, then the shot's own action. A scene's shot ACTION is the field that actually writes the clip — everything above it is context that gets prepended.
